chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh, may Allah have mercy upon him, narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Winter is the spring of the believer; its night is long, so he uses it to assist himself in his standing (in prayer).
ai.seo_question: Why is winter considered the believer's spring in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In *Sifat al-Shia*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the concept of *Rabi' al-Mu'min* (the believer's spring), where the extended darkness of winter nights serves as a spiritual opportunity for *Qiyam al-Layl*. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis oneness of night and day, contrasting the believer's spiritual vitality in winter with the potential distraction of summer's long days, thereby framing seasonal changes as divine mechanisms for worship.

en.badr-shahin: Mohammad bin Ali Majilwayh, Allah may have mercy upon him, narrated to us from… Mohammed bin Sulaiman ad-Dailami
that Abu Abdullah (a) said: Winter is the believer’s spring. Its long nights help the believer offer his rites of worship.
